correctness.rationale: A geometric nonsingularity test is proved equivalent to surjectivity of a 66-by-136 Macaulay matrix in degree ten using 3 generic base-point-free quartics and their Artinian regular sequence socle. The binary quartic restriction criterion is algebraically exact over the closure. All 32767 masks and all 168 projective changes are exhaustively processed; both embedded verifiers executed and agreed on smooth orbit representatives.

originality.rationale: Published general and asymptotic Bertini results, minimum-degree plane-filling classifications, and historical modular-quartic type results were compared by their actual mathematical implications. A complete joint rational-point/transverse-line histogram across all 10920 geometrically smooth binary plane quartics, with 78 line-profile projective orbits, was not identified in inspected research; the known plane-filling orbit is not claimed new. The key residual risk is whether the inaccessible Dickson 1915 treatments or a later table implicitly encode the same full profile.
residual_risks: Dickson 1915 follow-up and geometrical-invariantive primary full texts were not accessible; a historical complete table may implicitly entail some or all of the finite profile.
The 24 plane-filling transverse-free examples follow from Homma–Kim and are covered; only the complete distribution is asserted as original.
Semantic search and literature comparison cannot establish absolute priority, particularly for undigitized century-old research.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural finite-degree refinement of the published transverse-free Bertini probability problem in the first possible degree and smallest finite field, giving the entire rational-line spectrum, twenty arithmetic incidence strata and their 78 projective orbit decomposition. It is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a routine small correction; full uniform counting across canonical genus-three models is not determined by existence or asymptotic theorems.
